title: What If All the Water in the Sky Fell at Once?

scenes.text: What if every drop of water in the sky fell at once? It's far less than you'd guess.
The whole atmosphere holds about 13,000 cubic kilometers of water. That sounds huge, but it's roughly 0.001 percent of Earth's water.
Spread evenly over the planet, it would make a puddle about one inch deep. Two and a half centimeters, everywhere.
Nature does this constantly. About 1,580 cubic kilometers of water fall as rain and snow every single day.
So the sky's entire supply is only about eight days of rain. A water molecule stays up there roughly 8 to 9 days.
The sky is nearly empty and refills every week. You are always living under just an inch of rain.

description:
What if all the water in the sky fell at once?
The atmosphere holds about 13,000 cubic kilometers, which would cover Earth in roughly one inch of rain, and it refills in about eight days.
